bpLabel: Fieldstrip Best Practices — this guide follows the SKS field strip as documented in the United States Army’s own training circular for the SKS carbine (TC 9-56, 1969), the government manual for this rifle. It is not a manufacturer’s manual for this model. If you obtain a manual for your rifle from its maker or importer, follow it over this guide. Never take this firearm further apart than this guide goes.
cleanIntro:
No living maker publishes a manual for this model — the makers were arsenals, and the arsenals are gone. But the rifle itself is the pattern, and the United States Army documented its field strip in TC 9-56, the government’s own training circular for the SKS. This guide follows it. SKS carbines were built in several countries and small details differ — the East German guns carry no tool case or cleaning rod, for one — so where yours differs from a step, work with what your rifle has.

Listed in Fieldstrip as 7.62x39. The chambering marked on the gun itself is the one that counts — not this guide, and not the listing.

steps.title: Ammunition out of the room, muzzle somewhere safe
steps.action: Before you start, put every loose cartridge, loaded magazine and box of ammunition in another room — a cleaning bench with live rounds on it is where unintended discharges happen. Keep the muzzle pointed where a shot would hurt no one, and keep your finger outside the trigger guard the whole time. Wear eye protection whenever you use solvent or work near a spring, and work where the air moves.
steps.prose: A safety, if yours has one, is never a substitute for an empty chamber, and nothing in this guide relies on one.

steps.title: Clear the weapon — look and feel, twice
steps.action: Pull the operating handle fully rearward; on an empty magazine the bolt should catch open. Look into the chamber and down at the magazine follower, then put a fingertip to the chamber. If cartridges remain in the fixed magazine, open the magazine cover by its catch behind it and let them fall clear, then check chamber and magazine again. Do the whole check a second time, and keep your hand out of the bolt’s path when it closes.
steps.cite: TC 9-56, SKS Rifle, Simonov Type 56 — Training Circular 9-56 — Disassembly and Assembly, a.(1), p.5

steps.title: Tool case and cleaning rod off
steps.action: If yours carries them: press the cover in the butt plate to eject the combination tool case, then swing the cleaning rod’s head clear of the front sight base and draw the rod out forward. An East German Karabiner-S has neither — skip ahead.
steps.quote: pull the cleaning rod out of the rifle.
steps.cite: TC 9-56, SKS Rifle, Simonov Type 56 — Training Circular 9-56 — Disassembly and Assembly, a.(2), p.6

steps.title: Receiver cover pin out, cover and driving spring off
steps.action: Rotate the receiver cover pin — the knob at the right rear of the receiver — up to vertical and pull it out to the right as far as it goes; it may need a firm pry to start turning. Slide the receiver cover off to the rear, then draw the driving spring assembly out of the bolt carrier. The TC’s assembly step names the pin geometry this undoes.
steps.quote: Insure that the receiver cover pin is pulled fully out to the right, then slide the receiver cover into place from the rear.
steps.cite: TC 9-56, SKS Rifle, Simonov Type 56 — Training Circular 9-56 — Disassembly and Assembly, b.(4), p.8 — the assembly step for this same joint; removal is the motion reversed (the removal paragraph on p.6 does not extract cleanly from the scan)

steps.title: Carrier and bolt out, then apart
steps.action: Pull the operating handle fully rearward and lift the bolt carrier and bolt up and out of the receiver, then separate the bolt from the carrier. Note how the bolt sat — extractor to the right front — because it goes back exactly that way.
steps.quote: lift the bolt carrier and bolt out of the receiver. Separate the bolt from the bolt carrier.
steps.cite: TC 9-56, SKS Rifle, Simonov Type 56 — Training Circular 9-56 — Disassembly and Assembly, a.(4), p.6

steps.title: Gas tube up, piston out
steps.action: Rotate the gas cylinder tube lock up to its stop, lift the rear of the gas cylinder tube with its handguard, and the gas piston will slide out of it. Keep the piston with the tube.
steps.quote: lift the rear of the gas cylinder tube
steps.cite: TC 9-56, SKS Rifle, Simonov Type 56 — Training Circular 9-56 — Disassembly and Assembly, a.(5), pp.6-7

steps.title: And that is where it stops
steps.action: The TC’s next step — dropping the trigger group — is marked "if necessary", and on a surplus rifle on a kitchen bench it is not necessary: that is a qualified gunsmith’s work. The book closes the strip in its own words below.
steps.quote: (7) No further disassembly is necessary or desirable.
steps.cite: TC 9-56, SKS Rifle, Simonov Type 56 — Training Circular 9-56 — Disassembly and Assembly, a.(7), p.7

steps.title: Bore, gas system and bolt
steps.action: Brush the bore wet with solvent from the muzzle with a rod guide — or a pull-through from the chamber — then dry patches until clean and a lightly oiled patch for storage. Corrosive-primed surplus ammunition is common in this calibre: if any might have been fired, flush the bore, the gas piston, the piston channel and the bolt face with hot water or a water-based solvent first, dry everything, then oil. Wipe the carrier, the bolt and the inside of the receiver; the piston and tube go back dry.

steps.title: Look for the things that mean stop
steps.action: Hold the barrel up to the light and look through it: you want a clean, unbroken bore with no obstruction, no bulge and no dark ring. Look over the receiver, the barrel, the gas tube and the stock for cracks, a pitted or stuck gas piston, and for anything loose or missing. A screw or pin that has worked loose is reported, not tightened — how tight it should be is a question for a qualified gunsmith.
steps.prose: Any one of these means the gun is not fired until a qualified gunsmith has seen it.

deepAbsentReason: There is no deep clean for the Various (surplus) SKS, and this guide will not invent one. No living maker publishes a manual for this model; the pattern source documents a field strip and nothing deeper for an owner. Anything that needs more than this guide goes to a qualified gunsmith, not onto the bench.

cleaning.name: BORE
tasks: From the muzzle with a rod guide, or a pull-through from the chamber
After possibly-corrosive surplus ammunition: hot water or water-based solvent FIRST, then dry, then oil
A lightly oiled patch for storage; a dry patch before the next shot

cleaning.name: GAS SYSTEM & BOLT
tasks: Gas piston and tube wiped clean and put back DRY

cleaning.name: EXTERIOR
tasks: Wiped with a lightly oiled cloth
No solvent on wood, finishes or optics

cleaning.name: STORAGE
tasks: Stored dry — never shut in a closed case while damp
Looked over for rust at every clean

reassembly.title: Gas piston into its tube, tube locked down
reassembly.action: Slide the gas piston into the tube small end first, set the tube’s front over the gas cylinder, swing its rear into the rear sight base, and turn the lock back down.
reassembly.quote: Slide the gas piston, small end first, into the gas cylinder tube; fit the large end of the tube over the gas cylinder (fig 2 ).

reassembly.title: Bolt into the receiver, carrier mated over it
reassembly.action: Bolt into the receiver with the extractor to the right front, its rear about three-eighths of an inch off the receiver’s rear wall; carrier laid on top, pressed down and worked gently until it mates, then both slid fully forward.
reassembly.quote: Place the bolt into the receiver, with the extractor to the right front, and position the rear of the bolt about three-eights of an inch from the inner rear wall of the receiver.

reassembly.title: Driving spring in, stepped end first
reassembly.action: The driving spring assembly goes into the bolt carrier stepped end first.
reassembly.quote: stepped end first, into the bolt carrier.

reassembly.title: Cover on, pin rotated down to lock
reassembly.action: Cover pin pulled fully out to the right, cover slid into place from the rear, pin pushed home and rotated down. Cleaning rod and tool case back where they live.
reassembly.quote: Secure it with the receiver cover pin and rotate the pin down to the locked position.

fncheck: Chamber and magazine proven empty twice. Cycle the operating handle: the carrier runs fully back and returns fully to battery, and with the magazine empty and its follower up, the bolt catches open on the rearward stroke. The safety swings through its arc at the rear of the trigger guard. This check never asks you to press the trigger.
